fields.population: water-sector stakeholders in Sierra Leone: government ministries, departments and agencies (over 65% of participants), utilities (GUMA, SALWACO), regulators (e.g. NWRMA), donors and NGOs
fields.sample_size: 27 online-survey responses (snowball sampling) and 37 online semi-structured interviews in early 2025 (three participants did not complete the scoring task); desktop review of policy documents
fields.effect_measure: stakeholder analysis (STEEP framework; frequency of mention and normalised influence scores 1-5) and social network analysis of relationship strength and dependencies; qualitative themes
fields.effect_estimate: Fragmented governance with overlapping mandates; a tightly knit core of government MDAs, utilities and donors dominates, with peripheral and community stakeholders informed rather than empowered; heavy donor dependence with weak donor dependence on national institutions; network centrality is misaligned with functional authority (the Ministry is a central hub but strained; utilities are highly connected yet low-influence over economic/environmental policy; the regulator NWRMA bridges but lacks enforcement ties). Reforms (revised National WASH Policy, new regulatory bodies, ministry consolidation) are project-focused and siloed; the water crisis is described as a crisis of governance rather than scarcity. No effect estimate.
fields.model_type: stakeholder analysis and social network analysis with STEEP thematic analysis of interviews
fields.study_design: cross-sectional mixed-methods case study (desktop study, online survey with snowball sampling, semi-structured interviews with a scoring activity)
fields.risk_of_bias_rating: MMAT (re-appraised 2026-10-04 on the full text; supersedes the abstract-only rating of 2026-09-28). S1=Yes (aims stated); S2=Yes (data allow the questions to be addressed). Mixed-methods criteria: 5.1(rationale)=Yes (triangulation of desktop, survey and interview sources stated); 5.2(integration)=Yes (STEEP framework joined to network metrics, Section 3.5); 5.3(meta-inference)=Yes (Section 3.5 and conclusions); 5.4(divergence)=Yes (the optimistic quantitative scores versus the qualitative accounts are discussed, Section 3.6); 5.5(component quality)=Can't tell (over 65% government-affiliated participants, snowball sampling, 1-5 scoring that the authors say was 'disproportionately positive'; limitations acknowledged but not resolved). Per MMAT's own guide, no composite score is computed.

evidence_level: Single-study evidence: a cross-sectional mixed-methods governance and stakeholder analysis of Sierra Leone's water sector (27 survey responses, 37 interviews, social network analysis) read in full text 2026-10-04. Fragmented, donor-dependent governance with misaligned authority, capacity and network position; qualitative-quantitative divergence and over-representation of government participants acknowledged. No effect estimate.
